g: Grilling round 4 (2026-10-14): paying on arrival, choosing sellers, Tax tuning, bridges, shortcuts

q: Traders now pay when they arrive. What if the seller no longer has the Goods by then (another Trader got there first)?
o: The seller sets the Goods aside for that Trader when it leaves home, so they are always there on arrival (nobody else can buy them meanwhile)
The Trader buys whatever is left and carries the rest of its gold home
The Trader buys what is left, then drives on to the next seller for the rest

q: Choosing a seller, from your note: price against distance, with urgency, wealth and free Traders tipping it. Proposed rule: each seller gets a cost per unit = its price + (trip time × how much the Town values time). Time is worth more when the Town is starving for the Good, when it is rich, and when few of its Traders are free; the cheapest cost wins. If the need is big and Traders are free, it sends Traders to the next sellers too.
ctx: Example: Potato costs 6 gold at a Town 3 hexes away and 3 gold at a Town 12 hexes away. With 40 Potatoes in Stock the far Town wins (worth the wait). With 0 Potatoes the near one wins. With 3 of 4 Traders busy, the near one wins too.
o: Change it (say how in the note)

q: Tax tuning target. Today a Peasant at 70% happiness pays 12 gold a minute and uses 1.3 Potato + 0.9 Wood a minute (9.7 gold at base prices), so supplying them breaks even when the Town pays about 1.24× base. At 100% happiness with Fish and Wool: 19.2 gold a minute against 16.9 gold of Goods at base. Your rule: "can't always make a profit, but between base price and 1.5× it should even out". Which target do I tune every tier to (checked in the test runs)?
o: Break even at about 1.25× base price (today's Peasant numbers): profit when buying cheap, loss above 1.25×
Break even at 1.5× base: supplying residents almost always pays
Break even at base price: only cheap buys pay

q: Bridges are new (in your Tools tab). What is a bridge?
o: A road piece built on a water hex beside land, so Traders and Porters can cross narrow water; costs several times a road (proposal: 5×), Traders cross at road speed
Also a way through mountains (a pass)
